newsitem.title: THAILAND: Six killed in attack between rival Karen groups.
newsitem.headline: Six killed in attack between rival Karen groups.

text.p: At least six people were killed and seven others wounded when rival Karen guerrillas clashed in eastern Burma near the Thai border, Thai military and guerrilla sources said on Wednesday.

A Thai military source based on the border said heavy fighting broke out on Monday when the some 30 guerrillas from the Karen Nation Union (KNU) launched a surprise attack on the pro-Rangoon Democratic Karen Buddhist Army (DKBA) on the Burmese bank of the Moei river.
The Moei separates Burma and Thailand.
A KNU source confirmed the report and said at least six DKBA guerrillas were killed and seven others wounded. He would not reveal casualties on the KNU side.
The predominately Christian KNU was formed in 1948 after Burma became independent from Britain.
It is the last major rebel group left fighting for autonomy from Rangoon, despite several rounds of peace talks with Burma's military government.
THe DKBA, an offshoot of the KNU, was formed in late 1994 after a mutiny by a Buddhist faction from the core group.
